interfaces_and_contracts: The `README.md` section will document the following concrete interfaces, routes, tables, and environment variables verified in the checkout: 1. Generic event refusal and T1 goal capture: `POST /rooms/:roomId/events` refuses `GOVERNED_PATH_EVENTS` (`task.dispatched.planner`, `plan.submitted`, `plan.revision_requested`, `plan.approved`, `founder.cancel` in `packages/control-plane/src/governed-events.ts`, lines 27-33) before the ledger sees them. On T1 (`scope.captured`), `prepareFounderGoal` (`packages/control-plane/src/founder-goal.ts`, lines 50-73) checks an optional non-empty `goal` string (at most `FOUNDER_GOAL_MAX_LENGTH` of `20_000` characters, free of credential material via `containsCredentialMaterial`), rejects caller-supplied `founder_goal` evidence, and appends `{ kind: 'founder_goal', ref: event.eventId, digest: founderGoalDigest(goal) }`. 2. Plan judgement, storage, and read route: `judgePlanDoc` (`packages/control-plane/src/plan-doc.ts`, lines 36-56) validates against `PLANDOC_SCHEMA_V1`, checks canonical scope paths with `checkScopePaths`, computes `planHash` from `@build-room/journal`, and marks `readyForDecision` true only when `terminal_status` is `PLAN_READY_FOR_FOUNDER_APPROVAL`. Migration `0010_plan_store` (`packages/control-plane/src/migrations.ts`, lines 1875-1916) creates append-only table `public.build_room_plans` keyed by `command_id` with unique `(room_id, lifecycle_event_id)` referencing `public.build_room_events (room_id, event_id)` and grants only `SELECT, INSERT` to `br_app_runtime`. `PlanStore.recordPlan` (`packages/control-plane/src/plan-store.ts`, lines 189-251) requires that the referenced event is a committed T3 `plan.submitted` written by the current transaction (`e.xmin = pg_current_xact_id()::xid`) carrying the matching `plan_hash`, and scans all keys and string values with `containsCredentialMaterial`. `GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan` (`packages/control-plane/src/plan-read.ts`, lines 32-81), guarded by `CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN`, re-parses, re-judges, and recomputes `planHash` for the room's latest T3, returning `200 { roomId, commandId, planHash, document }`, `404` (`room_not_found` or `plan_not_found`), or `409 plan_changed` if superseded mid-read. 3. Founder plan-decision route: `POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan-decision` (`packages/control-plane/src/plan-decision.ts`, lines 417-482, body limit `PLAN_DECISION_BODY_LIMIT` `'64kb'`) is guarded solely by `PHASE3_ADJUDICATION_TOKEN` (answering `503 plan_decision_disabled` when unset). It accepts `decision` in `['plan.approved', 'plan.revision_requested', 'founder.cancel']`, `planHash` (required for approve/revise and for cancel in a plan-bearing state), `feedback` (required for `plan.revision_requested`, up to `FEEDBACK_MAX_LENGTH` of `20_000`), optional `eventId`, and `attribution: { actualModel, executionSurface }`. It commits the lifecycle transition (`actor: 'founder'`, `roleId: null`) and the journal decision record (`PLAN_DECISION_AUTHORIZATION_REF` `'founder-credential/PHASE3_ADJUDICATION_TOKEN'`) in one transaction. 4. Signed Gateway planner pull routes: `POST /gateway/planner/poll` (`GATEWAY_BODY_LIMIT` `'16kb'`) and `POST /gateway/planner/report` (`PLANNER_REPORT_BODY_LIMIT` `'256kb'`) in `packages/control-plane/src/gateway/routes.ts` (lines 171-201). 5. Counted-run routes and configuration: `POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/planner-round`, `GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/planner-round`, and `GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/journal` (`packages/control-plane/src/counted-run.ts`, lines 159-309) are guarded solely by `PHASE4_COUNTED_RUN_TOKEN` (`503 counted_run_disabled` when unset) and require `PHASE4_COUNTED_RUN` (`503 counted_run_not_configured` when unset). `parseCountedRunConfig` (`packages/control-plane/src/counted-run-config.ts`, lines 76-136) parses `{ actId, gatewayId, planner, seats: { builder, reviewer } }` where `planner` and `seats` name surfaces or `surface:provider` lane tokens (never models), requires `planner` surface `'antigravity'` (`COUNTED_RUN_PLANNER_SURFACE`), and enforces distinct surfaces and distinct providers between `builder` and `reviewer`. Starting a round also requires `RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_ID` and `build-room-control-plane` in the hash-pinned `packages/control-plane/fixtures/execution-surface-registry.md` (`COUNTED_RUN_REGISTRY.sha256` `060a16a40abb58794cf960d33010bee006e06d4f699f32f61704d1ecd88e2055`).
data_flow: The new section in `README.md` traces a Phase 4 planning round end to end as built: 1. Scope and Goal Capture (T1): A room captures scope via `scope.captured` with repository, `baseSha`, canonical scope paths, and a `goal` string whose SHA-256 digest is attached by `prepareFounderGoal` (`packages/control-plane/src/founder-goal.ts`, lines 50-73). 2. Round Opening (T2 or T4): `PlannerLoop.runRound(roomId)` (`packages/control-plane/src/planner-loop.ts`, lines 478-508) runs on a fenced `PostgresLedgerStore`. From `SCOPED`, `openFirstRound` (lines 541-585) locks the room, verifies the captured goal against its `founder_goal` digest, derives deterministic `commandId` via `plannerCommandIdFor(roomId, eventId, attempt)` in the `cmd_planner_` namespace (lines 160-169), and commits T2 `task.dispatched.planner` (`gatewayOnline` derived by the fence, `rolesAssigned` and `reviewerIsNotBuilder` derived from `roomRoles`) together with the command's `journaled` row (`commandKind` `'planner.invoke'`, `roleId` `'architect'`) in one transaction. From `PLANNING` after T4 `plan.revision_requested`, `openNextAttempt` journals the command under the room lock bound to T4 and attaches `revision: { feedback, revisingPlanHash, earlierPlan }` verified from `PlanStore`. 3. Pre-Contact Authorization and Attestation: Before any provider contact, the loop checks route coverage with `authorizeRoute` and calls `planner.attest(commandId)` over `GatewayPlannerChannel` (`packages/control-plane/src/gateway/planner-channel.ts`, lines 216-228). The assigned Gateway collects the `attest` request on `POST /gateway/planner/poll`, verifies the route locally in `GatewayPlannerWorker` (`packages/gateway-daemon/src/planner-worker.ts`), and answers `attested` on `POST /gateway/planner/report`. The loop then appends `identity_bound`. 4. Dispatch and Headless Execution: The loop calls `planner.dispatch(work)` (`planner-channel.ts`, lines 230-266). On the Gateway, `GatewayPlannerWorker` syncs a `starting` record to disk before invoking `AgyPlannerExecutor.start` (`packages/gateway-daemon/src/agy-planner-executor.ts`, line 771; `AgyPlannerExecutor` at lines 659-1411). `AgyPlannerExecutor` verifies the SHA-256 of the root-owned `agy` copy (`BUILDROOM_PLANNER_AGY_SHA256`), creates an anonymous read-only checkout of `repository` at `baseSha` under `BUILDROOM_PLANNER_CHECKOUTS`, spawns `sudo -n -u <plannerUser> -- <agyPath>` with `PINNED_AGY_ARGUMENTS` (`--input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --model gemini-4-argon-high --effort high --mode plan --sandbox --print-timeout 900s`), waits for the first stream-json `init` event, and writes the prompt to stdin only if `init.model === 'gemini-4-argon-high'` and after syncing its per-command evidence record. The Gateway reports `accepted` with `observed` route and `{ initModel, conversationId }`, and the control plane journals `dispatched` (`BRJ:c:2` carrying `initModel` and `providerConversationId`, required on the `antigravity`/`google` lane by `initRequired`). 5. Status Polling, Validation, Retries, and One Corrective Re-ask: `planner.awaitPlan(commandId)` polls `status` until the Gateway reports `finished`. On completion, `AgyPlannerExecutor` terminates `sudo`, runs `sudo -n -u <plannerUser> -- /usr/bin/pkill -KILL -u <plannerUser>`, verifies via `pgrep` that no planner-user processes remain, and removes the checkout. `judgeRoundPlan` checks `judgePlanDoc`, `PLAN_READY_FOR_FOUNDER_APPROVAL`, and that `repository`, `base_sha`, and `scope_paths` lie within captured T1 scope (`isWithinScope`). A `not_sent` attempt may be retried within `retryBudgetTransition` (`MAX_ROUND_ATTEMPTS = 1 + DISPATCH_POLICY.transport_retries_max`). Within a single `runRound` call, a round also gets at most one corrective re-ask when an attempt fails as `plan_invalid` (`schema`, `scope_path`, or `encoding`) or `planner_reported_failure` with a reason in `REASKED_FAILURE_REASONS` (`unparseable_plan`, `malformed_output`, `no_result`, `agy_error`, `oversize`). 6. Atomic Plan Submission (T3) and Founder Decision (T4/T5/T22): `submitRoundPlan` commits T3 `plan.submitted`, `PlanStore.recordPlan`, and the journal `completed` row (gated by the §5.3 completion authorization resolver) in one transaction. The Founder reads the plan via `GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan` and submits `plan.approved` (T5), `plan.revision_requested` (T4), or `founder.cancel` (T22) at `POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan-decision`.
trust_and_security_boundaries: The `README.md` section documents the following enforced trust and security boundaries: 1. Three separated control-plane tokens (`packages/control-plane/README.md`, lines 19-43): `CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN` (room routes and `GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan`), `PHASE3_ADJUDICATION_TOKEN` (`POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan-decision`, Founder-held and never given to the harness), and `PHASE4_COUNTED_RUN_TOKEN` (`POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/planner-round`, `GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/planner-round`, `GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/journal`). Each must be at least 32 characters in RFC 6750's token alphabet and distinct from the others at boot. 2. Server-derived guard facts: `POST /rooms/:roomId/events` blocks `GOVERNED_PATH_EVENTS` (`governed-events.ts`, lines 27-37). Every guard fact for T2, T3, T4, T5, and T22 (`rolesAssigned`, `reviewerIsNotBuilder`, `gatewayOnline`, `planDocSchemaValid`, `planHash`, `expectedPlanHash`, `scopePathsCanonical`, `feedbackAttached`, `runningTasksCancelled`, `unconfirmedCancelRecorded`) is derived by the server under the room lock and leadership fence, never accepted from caller input. 3. Pre-write credential guards and runtime role: `prepareFounderGoal`, `PlanStore.recordPlan`, `decidePlan`, and `JournalStore` scan strings with `containsCredentialMaterial` (`packages/journal/src/redact.ts`) before persistence. The control plane serves only as `br_app_runtime`, which holds only `SELECT, INSERT` on `public.build_room_plans` (`0010_plan_store`, lines 1913-1914) and appends to the journal only through `command_journal_append`. 4. Outbound-only Gateway pull channel and Linux planner isolation: The PC Gateway accepts no inbound connections (`planner-channel.ts`, lines 1-5); all planner requests flow over signed `POST /gateway/planner/poll` and `POST /gateway/planner/report` messages. `AgyPlannerExecutor` (`agy-planner-executor.ts`, lines 12-58) runs only on Linux Gateway `1880c12d-d98d-4a91-b25a-23320aa7f58a`, hashes the root-owned `agy` binary before every run, uses `PINNED_AGY_ARGUMENTS` (`--mode plan --sandbox`, with `BANNED_AGY_ARGUMENTS` rejected at module load), fetches public repositories anonymously into a read-only checkout,withholds the prompt until `init.model === 'gemini-4-argon-high'`, and reaps all planner-user processes after every run.

error_and_failure_behavior: The `README.md` section documents the fail-closed behavior built into each layer of the Phase 4 planner loop: 1. Generic route and goal refusals: posting any event in `GOVERNED_PATH_EVENTS` to `POST /rooms/:roomId/events` is refused before the ledger; supplying `founder_goal` evidence from a caller, attaching a `goal` to any event other than `scope.captured`, or supplying a blank, oversize (`> 20_000`), or credential-bearing `goal` throws `FounderGoalRefusedError` (`founder_goal_refused` in `founder-goal.ts`, lines 28-69). 2. Round failures vs. `unresolved`: `PlannerLoop` records a closed `PLANNER_FAILURES` classification (`authorization_does_not_cover`, `authorization_indeterminate`, `attestation_failed`, `identity_mismatch`, `not_sent`, `route_mismatch`, `planner_reported_failure`, `plan_invalid`, `plan_outside_captured_scope`, `plan_refused`, `completion_not_covered`, `round_superseded` in `planner-loop.ts`, lines 388-401) when a failure is determinable, and records `unresolved` whenever provider contact or completion coverage cannot be ruled out (`dispatch` or `awaitPlan` throwing, missing `init` fields on the `antigravity`/`google` lane, or indeterminate completion coverage). 3. Recovery (`planner-recovery.ts`, lines 148-260): `PlannerRecovery.recoverRoom` verifies the journal from genesis first (`journal.verify()`) and refuses recovery if verification fails; it reconciles open commands (`journaled`, `identity_bound`, `dispatched`, `unresolved`) by command ID via `planner.reconcile(commandId)` without re-executing or minting commands, leaving `ambiguous` or `mismatch` outcomes `unresolved`. 4. Gateway worker and executor halt (`planner-worker.ts`, lines 231-244 and 431-450; `agy-planner-executor.ts`, lines 43-57): `PlannerRecordStore` closes itself for the process lifetime on any fsync/write failure, and on restart `GatewayPlannerWorker.boot` (`packages/gateway-daemon/src/planner-worker.ts`, lines 431-450) marks a leftover `starting` record `not_sent` when the executor's own evidence says nothing was sent and `lost` otherwise, while a leftover `running` record becomes `lost` (so for `lost` records the worker stays silent and the control plane records `unresolved`). `AgyPlannerExecutor` writes `planner-halted.json` in the Gateway directory and refuses all further planner work if a planner-user process exists before start or survives `pkill -KILL -u <plannerUser>`, if `sudo` does not exit in time, if a checkout cannot be removed, or if an evidence record cannot be written or read.
